plan.title: spec: render produces unusably large SPECIFICATION.md by default

narratives.Description: spec: render produces unusably large SPECIFICATION.md by default
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

`task spec:render` currently produces an excessively large and unstable `SPECIFICATION.md` for directive and likely for long-lived consumer projects. The default renderer includes lifecycle scope aggregation from `vbrief/{pending,active,completed}`, so completed work history is dumped into the rendered product specification.

This makes the generated output difficult for humans and agents to use as a specification and creates recurring PR churn after lifecycle moves.

## Observed in directive

Current checked-in `SPECIFICATION.md`:

- About 8,567 lines
- About 939k characters

Rendering with the current default behavior:

- `task spec:render` succeeds
- Output grows to roughly 10k+ logical lines / about 1.2MB in the comparison run
- The diff adds thousands of lines from active/completed vBRIEFs
- Some embedded lifecycle issue bodies carry Markdown hard-break trailing spaces into the generated output

Rendering with scopes disabled:

- `uv run python scripts/spec_render.py vbrief/specification.vbrief.json SPECIFICATION.scopes-off.md --include-scopes=off`
- About 1,268 lines
- About 162KB
- Much closer to a usable product specification

## Root cause

`tasks/spec.yml` invokes `scripts/spec_render.py` with no flags. `scripts/spec_render.py` defaults `include_scopes=True` and appends an `Implementation Plan` section generated from all lifecycle folders, including `vbrief/completed`.

Directive currently has hundreds of completed vBRIEFs, so normal render becomes a lifecycle archive dump rather than a stable spec render.

## Suggested fix

- Make normal `task spec:render` compact and stable by default.
- Default lifecycle scope aggregation off.
- Add explicit opt-in flags/modes for lifecycle context, for example:
  - `--include-scopes=off` default
  - `--include-scopes=active` or `current` for pending/active only
  - `--include-scopes=all` for old behavior
- Add a separate lifecycle report command if full aggregation is still useful.
- Add an `--include-legacy-artifacts=on|off` option and default legacy artifacts off in rendered specs.
- Normalize rendered markdown trailing whitespace.
- Add tests proving completed lifecycle count does not bloat default `SPECIFICATION.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `task spec:render` produces a compact deterministic `SPECIFICATION.md` by default.
- Default render excludes completed lifecycle archive content.
- Default render excludes `LegacyArtifacts` from the visible specification unless explicitly requested.
- Existing lifecycle aggregation remains available via an explicit non-default option or separate report command.
- Rendered markdown has no trailing whitespace.
- Tests cover default compact behavior and explicit opt-in aggregation.

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-06-09T18:26:48Z)

## Additional PRD render finding

Follow-up from testing `task prd:render` after this issue was filed:

- The checked-in `PRD.md` is hand-authored, stale, and lacks the `AUTO-GENERATED by task prd:render` banner.
- Normal `task prd:render` correctly refuses to overwrite it because of the #539 non-generated-file safety guard.
- Rendering to a comparison file works:
  - current `PRD.md`: about 10KB / 94 lines
  - generated `PRD.generated.md`: about 115KB / 833 lines
- PRD render does not aggregate lifecycle folders like `spec:render`; its bloat comes from rendering all `plan.narratives` in `vbrief/specification.vbrief.json`, especially `LegacyArtifacts` (~105k chars / ~1,246 source lines).

## Scope addition

This issue should also make PRD rendering usable again after the spec render/source cleanup lands:

- Remove or archive the stale hand-authored `PRD.md` once the rendered source is fixed.
- Allow `task prd:render` to produce the canonical checked-in `PRD.md` again, with the generated banner.
- Ensure default PRD render excludes migration-era `LegacyArtifacts` unless explicitly requested.
- Add tests that `task prd:render` output stays compact and does not include legacy/archive material by default.

## Additional acceptance criteria

- `task prd:render` can regenerate the checked-in `PRD.md` after the spec/source cleanup without needing `--force` on a stale hand-authored file.
- Generated `PRD.md` has the standard machine-generated banner.
- Default generated `PRD.md` excludes `LegacyArtifacts` and remains compact.
- Legacy/audit PRD material remains available through an explicit opt-in or separate report if needed.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-06-11T15:39:02Z)

## Cross-link: spec reconstruction + drift-guard package depends on this

Tracked by #1589 (umbrella epic). Full design detail (Warp): https://app.warp.dev/drive/notebook/usS9x93ShZ38eFwfmziSsM

The package treats this issue as a prerequisite, not a duplicate. Reconstruction needs the compact, stable default `spec:render` this issue delivers - a reviewable baseline is impossible while the default render dumps `completed/` lifecycle (~8.5k lines / ~939KB). This issue lands first; reconstruction (and the #1567 refresh) build on it.
